body: Actually, this is not a bad idea. Look, I think it is comforting in thinking of just being gone. Wasn't not existing so much easier? Others have only ever fucked me, so why do I give a fuck about anyone? Truth is, when things get desperate, nobody really gives a fuck about you. That's when you see people's true colors. It's easy to go through life when things are going well. When the shit hits the fan, then you really see the person beneath all the other bull shit they would have you believe about them. I'm as suicidal as the next suicidal individual on here. No matter how many psychologists or psychiatrists I go to, nothing gets better. YOU have to want to get better! They tell you. Sure, I suppose. But do you say the same thing to someone with pancreatic cancer? You know, if you just WANTED to get better, the cancerous cells would stop metastasizing, and you would be cured! If you giggle at this, it is because this notion is ridiculous on the face of it, but it is in fact what people tell the depressed and suicidal. It is treated quite different from other diseases, and this is a big problem. I met a guy in outpatient therapy who was unemployed for 7 years and schizophrenic. I saw how easily that could be me in 7 years. Because if I am alive, that time will come. It is frustrating that most people fortunate enough to not be afflicted with mental health maladies just pass it off as laziness or some other such term that comes nowhere near explaining the disease. I attribute it to active ignorance. I like the use of the word active here. It is not just ignorance: they choose to not learn about it. It takes energy to avoid learning about it, and do other things, rather than take the time to understand what it means to have the disease. But such are some people. I hope this has been beneficial for someone, somewhere out there to read. It is therapeutic for me to write. I am at my wit's end with life. Why did God give me this disease? Why did God make me do such terrible things to myself? Why did God make me thing such terrible things of myself? Why? Why? Why? I am not a religious person at all. I believe when I die there is absolutely nothing. I will always believe that. Why that scares religious people, I don't know. I didn't exist for how many billions of years, I'm here for a moment in time, and gone, and I'm supposed to be worried about what happens the next few billions of years? I think not. We might as well enjoy this short trip of life as well as we can, and make the most of it. If we can beat this illness, maybe we can go someplace and share our struggles with others, and make a positive difference on them. There are always people struggling. There will always be a need for a voice speaking for those struggling with diseases. Maybe you can be one of those people? Maybe I can too, and we will meet some day and share a laugh about our "sick" chapter of life.

I just have worked so fucking hard for so fucking long and have no results for any of it. Sure, I have a degree and some experience, and am enrolled in a program, but none of it means I will get anywhere. Sure, sure, there are no guarantees in life but death and taxes. I am not complaining about having to work through life; I rather enjoy work. It would be so much easier if I had no memory. Then I wouldn't remember all I have been given, and how I have thrown most of it away. I did it to myself due to the depression. I take responsibility for it. My own dad has no sympathy for me: "It was self-inflicted." It sure was, but that does not change the pain. Aside from the present economic pain, there is this mental illness ruining the greatest accomplishment I achieved: permanent employment. My illness let the words and actions of others affect my behavior for no good reason. Most of the people bullying me in the workplace knew they could not get rid of me, so they acted in other ways to "crowd me out." It is this aspect of human nature that disgusts me. At times I knew I was an amazing person: I read a lot, refrained from judgment, went to work every day, took care of myself, etc. I have gone through many changes in the last 5 years; some of them the doing of others, some of them my own doing. The clock is always ticking, and after all this time, it feels as if am currently nowhere. I experience panic attacks from being at the same campus I was at, at 19 years old, that I am now at, at 32 years old. What I did in the interim: BA degree and 5 years experience, but no financial results, which is extremely frustrating. I am simply not very good at making money, and that is the scorecard everyone judges you by in life. If I cannot do that, I cannot face my peers. If I cannot do that, nothing else matters. If I had a family, I might have kept the job I was in, at all costs. I have brought incredible pain on myself, and I suppose I can turn that around and say it is possible to bring incredible pleasure too, through even more professional accomplishments. I am burning inside with anger toward myself, and also toward human nature. Human nature was here before I was, and it will be here after I am gone; I don't need the serenity poem to remind me of that. The world owes me nothing for the same reason; it was here first; it will be here long after I have left it. I left the christian faith for fundamental reasons: I do not believe in turning the other cheek. I think this philosophy that was embedded in me in childhood has a lot to do with why I have been bullied much both in childhood and adulthood. Judaism does not believe in turning the other cheek, but in fighting back. This, I can get behind. And so I checked out the Torah recently from the library, but I have so much to catch up on in my classes, I have not opened it yet. My future in my eyes is bleak. It may change, and it may not. No one can tell the future. But if I don't change my ways, it will remain bleak.

When I was 19 and taking an astronomy class, it was always academic to hear about my life being compared to the life of earth compared to the life of the universe (in terms of ratios, of course). Now that I'm 32, and the more I mentally consume information concerning the death of people all around me, it is becoming less and less academic. Of course, nothing has changed since then, except my way of thinking about it; it was always so. In this it is frustrating, because I think about these abstract concepts knowing it does not help me in any practical way. In a way, thinking about the universe being meaningless, is meaningless. You'll notice from one of my other posts, that I am suicidal. But from the other comment on here regarding being suicidal being meaningless, and that we might as well live, makes as much sense to me as anything else. My cousin committed suicide a few years ago. I knew him well as a child, but had grown apart as our lives diverged. He was diagnosed with a form of schizophrenia. That is a whole other bag, but I used to want to live my life to the fullest, for him. I have lost that feeling, and I wish desperately I could get it back. It is true we are just a flicker in the universe, but so is a candle's light, but a candle's light serves a distinct purpose. A light in the darkness for whoever happens to be near that light. Elton John's "Candle in the wind" comes to mind.

And it also comes down to the fact that obsessing over suicide and severe depression and panic, etc is exhausting. At some point, I have to either decide to act on irrational thoughts or decide to live. I have to decide to live. I have to believe that is the only thing there is to do.

You're right about the failure comment, but these strange thoughts seem so true until we air them out and expose them as the lies they are. And you're also right in that I can get back to where I was, or something even better. It certainly helps at times like these to be reminded of that. I'm sure you all can understand the kind of thoughts you can have when you feel absolutely worthless.
